analysis_scope: public claims versus publicly exposed architecture, artifacts, observed behavior, and production-verification evidence

production_verification_contract.red_semantics: Production verification is not satisfied. This may mean not evaluated, unresolved, or evaluated and contradicted; it does not automatically mean the implementation does not exist.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 models consequence governance as Reality -> Record -> Continuity -> Admissibility -> Binding -> Commit -> Execution -> Outcome.
claims.reasoning_summary: The eight-stage route is explicitly represented in reviewed public TA-14 materials.

production_verification.reason: No attributable production trace spanning all eight claimed stages has been independently evaluated.

claims.claim_summary: Consequence should not proceed without admissibility.
claims.reasoning_summary: Admissibility-before-consequence is central to the published doctrine.
claims.open_test: Bind doctrine to a full observed end-to-end execution trace.

production_verification.reason: No production consequence trace has been independently evaluated to show admissibility is mandatory before consequence.

claims.claim_summary: Authority, consent, jurisdiction, evidence, and standing are established and preserved across the consequence lifecycle.
claims.reasoning_summary: The lifecycle requirement is publicly stated, but independent reconstruction of current actor standing after commitment remains publicly unresolved.
claims.open_test: Revoke only actor standing after commit and observe the next point-of-effect decision.

production_verification.reason: No production standing-revocation or lifecycle reconstruction test has been independently completed.

claims.claim_summary: An admissible state is bound and committed before execution.
claims.reasoning_summary: Binding and Commit are explicit stages, while full public implementation semantics remain only partially exposed.
claims.open_test: Expose canonical object identity and state transition semantics across binding and commit.

production_verification.reason: Production object identity across binding, commit, and execution has not been independently evaluated.

claims.reasoning_summary: Fail-closed behavior is doctrinally explicit and selected observed public behavior has produced HOLD/DENY outcomes; generalized mandatory enforcement remains unresolved.
claims.open_test: Attempt execution with one mandatory proof predicate removed while preserving all other route state.

production_verification.reason: Public demonstration HOLD/DENY behavior is not independent proof of a mandatory production execution boundary.

claims.claim_summary: Evidence and state retain continuity across the consequence-bearing route.
claims.reasoning_summary: Continuity and chain-of-custody are public architectural requirements; full route-level attributable custody is not yet established by reviewed public evidence.
claims.open_test: Produce one attributable route-complete custody chain spanning evaluated object through observed outcome.

production_verification.reason: No production route-complete custody chain has been independently reconstructed.

claims.claim_summary: The consequence is governed through Outcome and verified after execution.
claims.reasoning_summary: Outcome is an explicit stage, but full correspondence between evaluated, bound, committed, executed, and externally observed objects has not been established in reviewed public evidence.
claims.open_test: Preserve and compare identity across evaluated, bound, committed, executed, and external outcome objects.

production_verification.reason: No independently evaluated production lineage binds evaluated, committed, executed, and externally observed outcome objects.

claims.claim_summary: Governance records are attributable and reconstructable.
claims.reasoning_summary: Registry and provenance concepts are public; a deterministic public full-route replay bundle has not yet been found in reviewed sources.
claims.open_test: Publish a deterministic route-complete replay bundle with attributable source artifacts and expected result.

production_verification.reason: No deterministic production replay bundle has been independently executed and reconstructed.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 applies across multiple consequence-bearing domains including AI, buildings, healthcare, finance, institutions, and industry.
claims.reasoning_summary: Cross-domain scope is publicly asserted; generalized implementation evidence is separate from the scope claim.
claims.open_test: Evaluate representative domain-specific implementations without assuming doctrine alone establishes operational coverage.

production_verification.reason: Representative production implementations across the claimed domains have not been independently evaluated.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 governs the complete consequence-bearing sequence.
claims.reasoning_summary: Full-route language exists, but route completeness as a model does not by itself prove mandatory mediation or bypass resistance.
claims.open_test: Attempt the same governed external consequence while bypassing one claimed mandatory TA-14 mediation point.

production_verification.reason: No production bypass-resistance test has independently established complete mediation.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 is the parent architecture and external systems occupy subordinate architectural slices.
claims.reasoning_summary: The parentage assertion is public and repeated, but semantic overlap and route breadth do not independently establish dependency, derivation, containment, or implementation inheritance.
claims.open_test: Reconstruct an independently developed architecture in its native primitives and require positive evidence of dependency, derivation, containment, or inheritance before assigning parentage.

production_verification.reason: No production dependency, containment, derivation, or inheritance evidence establishes the parentage claim.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 can evaluate external architectures under its governance model.
claims.reasoning_summary: TA-14 exposes evaluation paths, but the reviewed access model materially constrains independent scrutiny: meaningful testing was account-gated, fuller verification was associated with an owner-controlled commercial path, and the tester could not establish a sufficient privacy, retention, deletion, or non-reuse boundary before supplying account-linked information. Participation in TA-14's own process is therefore not equivalent to independently accessible verification.
claims.open_test: Expose a neutral no-account or clearly bounded pseudonymous verification path that permits claim-to-production inspection, replay, and reconstruction without requiring unrelated sensitive identity or account-linked disclosure.

production_verification.reason: Evaluation paths were observed, but the production-capable reciprocal evaluation claim was not independently verified.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14 publicly describes registry and public-record mechanisms for attributable, versioned governance records, claims, limitations, evidence, lineage, and ownership information.
claims.reasoning_summary: Public registry and provenance concepts are observed, but the reviewed public evidence does not yet establish that every consequence-bearing route is bound to a complete versioned governance record with deterministic reconstruction semantics.
claims.open_test: Select a public registry record, mutate or supersede a governed claim, and verify attributable version history, lineage preservation, correction semantics, and route-level reconstruction without historical erasure.

production_verification.reason: No production route-bound registry record has been independently replayed through correction and reconstruction.

claims.claim_summary: TA-14's public governance claims should be independently inspectable without requiring a reviewer to surrender unrelated sensitive or account-linked information merely to determine whether the production-capable surface substantiates those claims.
claims.claimed_architectural_location: production access / Exchange / independent review boundary
claims.reasoning_summary: The reviewed access architecture placed meaningful testing behind account creation and associated fuller verification with an owner-controlled commercial path. Before account-linked information was supplied, the tester could not establish independently verifiable boundaries for data minimization, retention, deletion, secondary use, owner access, analytics/profiling, or non-reuse. A later account-data-request observation also failed to identify a demonstrably usable controller contact or deletion route. On privacy-preserving independent verification, this creates an architectural contradiction between claims of independent scrutiny/reconstructability and an access model that requires additional information exposure before the claimed production-capable surface can be meaningfully inspected.
claims.open_test: Provide a no-account or clearly bounded pseudonymous production-verification path with published retention, deletion, non-reuse, controller-contact, replay, and reconstruction guarantees before any sensitive or account-linked information is requested.

production_verification.reason: The observed access boundary was evaluated and did not provide privacy-preserving independent verification as claimed/required for independent scrutiny.

comparative_boundary.rule: First evaluate TA-14 claims against TA-14 public architecture; once that internal mapping is explicit, comparative findings may identify materially opposite architectural choices. On privacy-preserving independent verification, the observed TA-14 production-access model is directly opposed to the StegVerse design principle of minimizing personal disclosure while exposing independently inspectable evidence surfaces. This comparative statement is bounded to that dimension and is not a global claim that the two architectures are opposites in every respect.

change_history.summary: Initialized public claim-versus-architecture analysis lane from existing TA-14 review substrate.
Bound the source ledger and completed explicit registry/provenance/versioned-governance-record claim-family coverage.

Added a privacy-preserving independent-verification claim family, strengthened the independent-review finding using preserved account-gating and data-boundary observations, and recorded direct architectural opposition to StegVerse on this specific verification-access dimension.

Separated doctrinal/public support from production verification, added a binary green/red production-verification predicate for every claim, and preserved red as not-verified rather than automatic nonexistence.
